title: What was that mysterious object being transported along North Lindbergh? Boeing explains
content:
Jennifer Somers

Updated

Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:14 PM UTC

1 min read

A mysterious object being transported Sunday night along North Lindbergh Boulevard caught the attention of drivers and sparked speculation on social media.

Escorted by vehicles with flashing lights, the slow-moving truck carried an unusual-looking object that had people guessing. Was it a spaceship, part of an aircraft or a giant drone?

According to Boeing, it was an MQ-25 Stingray unmanned aircraft.

The MQ-25 Stingray is "the U.S. Navy's first operational, carrier-based unmanned aircraft. Built to operate from aircraft carriers, its primary mission is unmanned aerial refueling to extend the range, endurance, and flexibility of the carrier air wing," according to the company's website.

A spokesperson for Boeing said the aircraft was moved from the company's Berkeley, Missouri, facility to its new MQ-25 production facility near the MidAmerica Airport in Mascoutah, Illinois.

The move was coordinated with the Missouri and Illinois departments of transportation, Missouri State Highway Patrol, Illinois State Police and a U.S. Navy partner to ensure the aircraft was transported safely, the spokesperson said.

Boeing said the MQ-25 is the second aircraft to begin production at the new Mascoutah facility.

Another MQ-25 transport caught drivers' attention in 2019.
